newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM gold firm, platinum mixed after quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM gold firm, platinum mixed after quiet trade.

text.p: Yen-based gold futures ended firmer after drifting sideways on Tuesday, while platinum prices were mixed as private investors were taking profits in distant months after recent price gains, traders said.
Activity was quiet ahead of the Christmas holidays in overseas markets.

Gold prices ranged from one to six yen per gram higher, with most-active benchmark December ending up three at 1,347 yen. Platinum prices ranged from five yen per gram lower to eight yen firmer, with benchmark December finishing down three at 1,358 yen.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $368.90/369.40 per ounce at 0739 GMT, against $368.60/369.10 in New York on Monday.

"In the gold futures market, individual investors rolled over their long positions from the October contract to the December contract. Except for that, trading was dominated by inter-month trade by trade houses," one senior dealer at a foreign bank said.
Traders said they expected spot gold to be steady to firmer for the rest of this year on technical-led short-covering, but the resistance at $370 could be tough to break through.

For platinum, the recent widening gold/platinum spread prompted investors to take profits of distant months in platinum futures, although uncertainty concerning the delay in Japan-Russia talks for platinum export contracts remained, the traders said.
Palladium futures were lower across the board, weighed down by weaker spot prices. Benchmark December palladium was down three yen per gram at 430 yen.
Benchmark December silver was 0.2 yen per 10 grams up at 179.8 yen.
